Area.evidence_source: As participants disconnected themselves more and more both from their sources of support and from stressful situations, they described losing a sense of identity and a sense of a future. For example, Johan said 'you kinda lose direction', 'lose track of longsight' and 'suddenly feel like you are running in a circle'. Suicide was perceived as an opportunity to experience autonomy – having the capacity to reach a desired outcome. All participants indicated that they became curious about death rather than terrified of it. Brian said that he and his friends wondered 'if earth itself isn't hell' and what it would feel like to be dead. Similarly, Andrew said: 'I was experimenting with drugs a lot and then I just had this curiosity of what it would be like to die.' He engaged in high-risk behaviour as a means of killing himself, but avoiding being blamed by others for it: So you are getting into high risk behaviour – you don't want it to be your fault, you are looking for something to happen. I got into a lot of situations … I always felt afterwards that I was being kept alive. I wrote off two cars. I would start drinking and … then I would look for this high risk behaviour. Despite describing how they attempted to disconnect from their emotions, all participants reported becoming overwhelmed by their emotions and thoughts. For example, Mark said 'all the thoughts are coming in at one moment and it's craziness, you know. That kind of always leads to this [wanting to kill myself]'. They said that the fantasy of escaping their confused mind and painful emotions pushed them to act on their suicidal wishes. For example, Johan felt deeply ashamed for not taking any of his semester exams and he thought to himself, 'well, what if I disappear, then it all goes away'. All participants explained that while suicide was an attack against themselves, their suicide attempt was also interpersonally motivated. For Andrew and Johan suicide was not only an escape from self, but also a way of escaping what they perceived as negative evaluations from others. Johan said that he was motivated to attempt suicide to hide his failures and appear in control: 'No one has to know that I actually basically failed this year. No one has to ever find out. You know, it would be my little secret.' Mark and Brian explained that their suicide attempt was a form of communication and rebellion: I think of doing this [suicide] and those people are gonna miss me and they are gonna miss me … I wanted somebody to see my pain. I don't know who. I probably wanted everyone to see, especially all my friends probably. (Mark) I was really pissed with my parents, especially my dad. My room is sort of very dark. When I came home one day my dad had removed all my stuff and there was light. I was absolutely furious and I didn't know what to do. I was angry for starters and then I just thought 'Do this now!' (Brian)
